is

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: If m is the mass of an electron, h is the Planck's constant and a₀ is the radius of first orbit of H-atom, then kinetic energy of electron in the third orbit of He⁺ ion is given by (h²/(π² ma₀²)) · (1/x). What is the value of x?
B.sol_text:
Angular momentum of an electron in n^th orbit of a Bohr atom is given by
mvr = n(h/2π)

For an electron in 3rd orbit of He⁺ ion,
mv₃r₃ = 3(h/2π)
mv₃ = (3h)/(2πr₃)

r₃ = ((3)²a₀)/2 = (9a₀)/2

∴ mv₃ = (3h × 2)/(2π × 9a₀) = h/(3πa₀)

KE = (mv₃)²/(2m) = h²/(2m × 9π²a₀²) = (h²/(π²ma₀²))(1/18)

∴ x = 18

Given (1 - x³)ⁿ = Σ(k=0 to n) a_k x^k (1-x)^(3n-2k),
then the value of 3a_(k-1) + a_k is_____
A.sol_text:
Given [(1-x)(1+x+x²)]ⁿ = Σ(k=0 to n) a_k x^k (1-x)^(2k)

⇒ [(1+x+x²)/(1-x)²]ⁿ

= Σ(k=0 to n) a_k (x^k)/((1-x)^(2k))

⇒ [((1-x)²+3x)/(1-x)²]ⁿ

= Σ(k=0 to n) a_k (x/(1-x)²)^k

⇒ [1 + (3x)/(1-x)²]ⁿ = Σ(k=0 to n) a_k (x/(1-x)²)^k

Put (x)/((1-x)²) = t

⇒ (1+3t)ⁿ = Σ(k=0 to n) a_k t^k

Now 3a_(k-1) + a_k = 3·(coeff. of t^(k-1)) + coeff. of t^k
= 3·3^(k-1)·ⁿC_(k-1) + 3^k·ⁿC_k = 3^k[ⁿC_(k-1) + ⁿC_k]
= 3^k·ⁿ⁺¹C_k

A.text: Let x ∈ [-5π/12, -π/3]. Then the maximum value of y = tan(x + 2π/3) - tan(x + π/6) + cos(x + π/6) is
A.sol_text:

Solution:
Answer (3)

Let z = -x - π/6, then z ∈ [π/6, π/4]

∴ tan(x + 2π/3) = -cot(x + π/6) = cot z

y = cot z + tan z + cos z = 2/(sin 2z) + cos z

But 2/(sin 2z) and cos z are monotonic decreasing.

∴ Maximum value is at z = π/6

y_max = 2/(sin π/3) + cos π/6 = (11/6)√3

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The sequence {aₙ} is defined by a₀ = 1, a₁ = 1 and aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + (aₙ₋₁²)/(aₙ₋₂) for n ≥ 2, and the sequence {bₙ} is defined by b₀ = 1, b₁ = 3, and bₙ = bₙ₋₁ + (bₙ₋₁²)/(aₙ₋₂) for n ≥ 2. Then the value of b₅₀/a₅₀ is equal to
A.sol_text:
Answer (1)
∴ aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + (aₙ₋₁²)/(aₙ₋₁)
⇒ aₙ/(aₙ₋₁) = (aₙ₋₁)/(aₙ₋₂) + 1
It follows that: aₙ/(aₙ₋₁) = 1 + (aₙ₋₁)/(aₙ₋₂) = ...... = (n-1) + a₁/a₀ = n
and bₙ/(bₙ₋₁) = n - 1 + (b₁)/(b₀) = n + 2.
⇒ aₙ = n·aₙ₋₁ and bₙ = (n+2)·bₙ₋₁ respectively.
∴ aₙ = n! and bₙ = ((n+2)!)/2
∴ b₅₀/a₅₀ = (52!/2)/(50!) = (52×51)/2 = 26 × 51
= 1326

A.text: If (1 + x)^n = C_0 + C_1x + C_2x^2 + C_3x^3 + .... + C_nx^n, then the value of C_0^2 + (1+2)/2 C_1^2 + (1+2+3)/3 C_2^2 + ... up to n terms is equal to (where C_r = ^nC_r)
A.sol_text:
Answer: (4)
Hint:
Properties of binomial coefficients.

Solution:
∵(1 + x)^n = C_0 + C_1x + C_2x^2 + ... + C_nx^n
∴x(1 + x)^n = xC_0 + C_1x^2 + C_2x^3 + .... + C_nx^(n+1)

On differentiating both sides w.r.t. x we get
(1 + x)^n + nx(1 + x)^(n-1) = C_0 + 2C_1x + 3C_2x^2 + ... + (n + 1)C_nx^n  ....(1)

and (x + 1)^n = C_0x^n + C_1x^(n-1) + C_2x^(n-2) + ... + C_n  ....(2)

Multiply equation (1) and (2) and comparing the coefficient of x^n from both sides.
we get, C_0^2 + 2C_1^2 + 3C_2^2 + ... + (n + 1)C_n^2
= coefficient of x^n in [(1 + x)^(2n) + nx(a + x)^(2n-1)]
= ^(2n)C_n + n . ^(2n)C_(n-1)
∴ 2C_1^2 + 3C_2^2 + ... + (n + 1)C_n^2
= ^(2n)C_n(1 + (n/2)) - 1

C_0^2 + (1+2)/2 C_2^2 + ... + (1+2+...+n)/n C_n^2
= (1/2){^(2n)C_n((n/2) + 1) - 1}

B.text:
The least positive integral value of x satisfying (e^x − 2)(sinx − cosx)(x − ln2)
(cosx − 1/√2) > 0 is
B.sol_text:
(e^x − 2) and (x − ln2) both factors have same polarity.
S = (e^x − 2)(x − ln2)(sinx − cosx)(cosx − 1/√2)

0 ≤ x < π/4,
sinx < cosx and cosx > 1/√2 ⇒ S < 0

π/4 < x < 5π/4,
sinx > cosx and cosx < 1/√2 ⇒ S < 0

5π/4 < x < 7π/4,
sinx < cosx and cosx < 1/√2 ⇒ S > 0

For S > 0, least positive integral value of x is 4.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text:
If
cos α + cos β + cos γ = 0 = sin α + sin β + sin γ
and
cos² α + cos² β + cos² γ = λ₁,
sin² α + sin² β + sin² γ = λ₂ cos(2α − β − γ) + cos(2γ − α − β) = λ₃
cos(α − β) + cos(β − γ) + cos(γ − α) = λ₄
then the absolute value of 4λ₁ + 6λ₂ + 7λ₃ − 8λ₄ is
B.sol_text:
Let x = cos α + i sin α, y = cos β + i sin β, z = cos γ + i sin γ
Now x + y + z = 0 ⇒ x² + y² + z² = 0 ⇒
⇒ cos 2α + cos 2β + cos 2γ = 0
⇒ cos² α + cos² β + cos² γ = 3/2 and sin² α + sin² β + sin² γ = 3/2
∴ λ₁ = 3/2, λ₂ = 3/2
Again x + y + z = 0
x³ + y³ + z³ = 3xyz
⇒ (x²)/(yz) + (y²)/(xz) + (z²)/(xy) = 3 ⇒ cos(2α − β − γ) + cos(2β − γ − α) + cos(2γ − α − β) = 3
⇒ λ₃ = 3
again, cos α + cos β = − cos γ
and sin α + sin β = − sin γ
squaring and adding, cos(α − β) = −(1/2)
∴ cos(α − β) + cos(β − γ) + cos(γ − α) = −(3/2)
⇒ λ₄ = −(3/2)
∴ 4λ₁ + 6λ₂ + 7λ₃ − 8λ₄ = 6 + 9 + 21 + 12 = 48
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.
